Definition: to reside or permanently stay (literally or figuratively)
BiblicalUsage: Shakan is to dwell and stay put, to take up residence and remain. God told Israel to make Him a sanctuary that He might dwell among them, and promised Solomon He would dwell among the children of Israel and not forsake them. Isaiah lifts the word to heaven itself, for the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity dwells with him who is of a contrite and humble spirit, and the psalm asks who shall dwell in His holy hill.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe dwelling is God's great promise, that He does not visit and leave but stays. He dwells in the high and holy place and with the humble at the same time, and that is the whole gospel in one word. That is why I seek His presence, because He has promised to dwell with the contrite.
